preamble: Fortition of the palatal glide [j] to a velar stop [ɡ]. The classic case is Holtzmann's law (Verschärfung) in North Germanic, where the Proto-Germanic geminate glide *-jj- hardened to -ggj- (Gothic -ddj-), as in *ajją > Old Norse egg 'egg'. A later parallel is Faroese skerping, where a hiatus glide after a high vowel hardened to -ggj- (Old Norse þrír > Faroese tríggir 'three').

examples.note: Holtzmann's law: geminate *-jj- hardened to a velar stop in North Germanic; cf. Crimean Gothic ada (-ddj- in East Germanic) and the unhardened West Germanic Old High German ei, Old English ǣġ.
Skerping: a glide arising in hiatus after a high vowel hardened to -ggj-, a later Nordic parallel to Holtzmann's law.
